blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Managing the players in your supply chain is half relationship, half discipline. Each supplier, each carrier, each warehouse partner is a small business with its own priorities. Your job is to get the outcome you need while keeping the relationship healthy enough that they will pick up the phone when you call at 7 a.m. with a problem.

Three habits help. Communicate early and honestly: when something changes on your side, tell them before they find out. Pay on time, without drama. And recognise good work quietly, even when no one is watching.

The partners who trust you are the ones who will help you out of trouble. The ones who feel squeezed become the ones who enjoy watching you struggle. Which side you are on is almost always your choice.

items.q: According to the text, how is managing supply chain players best described?
options: Mostly a legal and contractual task
Purely a matter of price negotiation
items.why: "Managing the players in your supply chain is half relationship, half discipline."

items.q: What are the three habits the text recommends?
options: Meet weekly, sign contracts, track metrics
Communicate early, pay on time, recognise good work
Negotiate hard, audit often, switch suppliers
items.why: "Communicate early and honestly… Pay on time… recognise good work quietly."

items.q: When something changes on your side, the text says you should…
options: tell them before they find out
items.why: "when something changes on your side, tell them before they find out."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Trust makes partners more willing to help in a crisis.
How you treat partners is largely your own choice.
A squeezed supplier may quietly enjoy your problems.
Squeezing suppliers hard is the smartest way to secure their loyalty.
items.why: Inferência: o texto contrasta parceiros que confiam (ajudam) com os que se sentem pressionados (torcem contra) — pressionar não gera lealdade.

items.q: The detail about recognising good work "even when no one is watching" suggests that…
options: recognition should be given only in public
sincere recognition matters more than being seen giving it
quiet praise is a waste of effort
items.why: Inferência: reconhecer sem plateia mostra que o gesto é genuíno, não performance para os outros.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver revendo uma relação com fornecedor que esfriou. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So I pulled up the file on this supplier, and honestly, the relationship has gone cold over the last six months. Nothing dramatic — no argument, no missed delivery. It just quietly stopped working, and I wanted to understand why.

I found three breakdowns, and all three are on us. First, we changed our forecast twice without telling them. They only found out when the order volume didn't match what we'd agreed, so they were planning against numbers that were already wrong.

Second, our finance team stretched two invoices out to sixty days with no explanation. From their side, that reads as a signal — that we don't value them, or that we're in trouble ourselves.

And third, they hit every deadline through a difficult quarter, and not one of us said thank you. Small thing, but people remember it.

None of these is expensive to fix. I'm going to call their account manager this afternoon, walk through all three honestly, and settle the invoices this week. If we want them picking up the phone when we need a favour, we have to be the kind of partner worth answering.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Oliver describe what happened to the supplier relationship?
options: It ended in a serious argument
It collapsed after a missed delivery
It quietly went cold over six months
It improved once prices were renegotiated
items.why: "the relationship has gone cold over the last six months. Nothing dramatic… It just quietly stopped working."

items.q: What was the FIRST breakdown Oliver found?
options: The supplier raised prices without warning
Oliver's side changed the forecast twice without telling them
items.why: "we changed our forecast twice without telling them."

items.q: Why does the sixty-day payment delay matter, according to Oliver?
options: It reads as a signal that we don't value them or are in trouble
It cost the supplier money in interest
items.why: "that reads as a signal — that we don't value them, or that we're in trouble ourselves."

items.q: When Oliver says all three breakdowns are "on us", he means…
options: his own company is responsible for them
the costs fall on his company
items.why: Inferência: "on us" = a culpa/responsabilidade é do lado dele, não do fornecedor.

items.q: What does Oliver's closing line reveal about his goal?
options: He wants to replace the supplier soon
He mainly wants to reduce costs
He wants to be a partner the supplier will help when needed
He wants to avoid contact for a while
items.why: Inferência: "we have to be the kind of partner worth answering" — o objetivo é reconstruir confiança para ter ajuda no futuro.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Every supplier is a small business with its own priorities." Priorities are…
options: the things that matter most to them
items.why: Priority = prioridade: aquilo que vem primeiro, o que mais importa.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Your job is to get the ___ you need without damaging the relationship."
items.why: Outcome = resultado: o que você precisa conseguir ao final.

items.q: "The supplier felt squeezed after two late payments." Squeezed here means…
items.why: Squeezed = pressionado, espremido: sob pressão financeira ou comercial.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When your forecast changes, warn the partner ___, before they find out on their own."
items.why: Early = cedo: avisar com antecedência, antes que descubram sozinhos.

items.q: "Trust is built through steady habits, not grand gestures." A habit is…
items.why: Habit = hábito: um comportamento regular e repetido, como pagar em dia e comunicar cedo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem na gestão de fornecedores. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "They will always pick up the phone when we call with a problem." To pick up the phone here means to…
options: be willing to respond and help
transfer the call to another team
items.why: Pick up the phone = atender/estar disponível para ajudar quando você precisa.

items.q: "A trusted partner will help you out of trouble when a shipment fails." This means they will…
options: get you out of a difficult situation
report the failure to your boss
items.why: Help you out of trouble = tirar você do aperto, ajudar numa situação difícil.

items.q: "We need to follow through on the promises we made to the carrier." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = cumprir até o fim o que foi prometido.

items.q: "Finance stretched out the invoices to sixty days." To stretch out a payment means to…
items.why: Stretch out = esticar/prolongar o prazo antes de pagar.

items.q: "A quiet thank-you can go a long way with a loyal supplier." This means it will…
options: take a long time to arrive
items.why: Go a long way = render muito, ter um efeito grande em relação ao esforço.
